title: Pullback naturality of the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $X,Y$ be schemes of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p], let $u:X\to Y$ be a morphism, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient sheaves $A_X,A_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the derived module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with the canonical identification $u^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For $T=X,Y$, let $F_T:T\to T$ be absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] and let
$$
\tau_T^{(b)}:L(F_T^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)},\qquad b\geq0,
$$
be the canonical trivialization induced by the relative Frobenius isomorphisms $r_{V/T}^{(b)}=(F_V^b,v):V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\times_{T,F_T^b}T$ for weakly etale objects $v:V\to T$: restriction along these isomorphisms identifies direct image by $F_T^b$ with the identity, the adjoint identification gives the inverse-image trivialization of module sheaves (the coefficient identification being that of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]), and the inverse image being exact, it induces $\tau_T^{(b)}$ termwise on complexes. For $b=1$ this specifies the canonical trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]; $\tau_T^{(0)}$ is the identity.

Using the canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the equality $uF_X^b=F_Y^bu$ gives the pullback-composition identification
$$
 c_{u,b}:Lu^*L(F_Y^b)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_X^b)^*Lu^*.
$$
As natural transformations on $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ one has
$$
 (\tau_X^{(b)}Lu^*)\circ c_{u,b}=Lu^*\tau_Y^{(b)}.
$$
Moreover, for integers $b_1,b_2\geq0$ and $T=X,Y$, the trivialization $\tau_T^{(b_1+b_2)}$ equals the composite
$$
 L(F_T^{b_1+b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(F_T^{b_1})^*L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_1)}L(F_T^{b_2})^*}L(F_T^{b_2})^*\xrightarrow{\tau_T^{(b_2)}}\operatorname{id},
$$
whose first arrow is the composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $F_T^{b_1+b_2}=F_T^{b_2}\circ F_T^{b_1}$; in particular $\tau_T^{(b)}$ is the $b$-fold iterate of $\tau_T^{(1)}$.
